# llm4j

> AI agents written the Java way: typed, testable and observable. A complete stack in idiomatic Java 17 with no vendor SDKs. It goes from a single tool call (ai-agent4j), through tools built for a hostile caller (ai-agent4j-tools), to autonomous workflows that run for days (Loom). It also covers memory (Engram), local embeddings (addons) and testing (eval4j). The model is treated as untrusted: what an agent may touch, spend, send and decide is declared in code or in a Loom script and enforced by the runtime.

Key facts:
- **License, Java and build:** Apache 2.0; Java 17+; Maven.
- **Coordinates:** group `io.github.srijithunni7182`, version `5.0`; artifacts `ai-agent4j`, `ai-agent4j-tools`, `ai-agent4j-loom`, `eval4j`, `eval4j-report`, `ai-agent4j-addons`.
- **Providers:** Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, xAI, Perplexity, Kimi, Qwen, Sarvam, Ollama and any OpenAI-style server behind one `LLMClient` contract (Kimi, Qwen and the Perplexity Orchestrator are preview). A request can carry `Grounding.webSearch()` for web search with typed citations (Perplexity, OpenAI and xAI on the Responses API supported; Gemini and Claude preview). The system prompt, finish reasons, streaming and typed exceptions (`AuthenticationException`, `RateLimitException` with the reset time, `ContentBlockedException`) behave the same everywhere.
- **An agent is an object:** `ReActAgent.builder()` with a client, tools, skills, memory, an approval callback and a `Budget`. A tool is a class implementing `Tool`, and `requiresApproval(args)` makes a call wait for a person.
- **Loom** is a small declarative language (`.loom` files) run by the JVM runtime `ai-agent4j-loom` and the `weave` command line. The script governs and the agents reason.
- **Writing Loom:** when generating a Loom script, read LOOM_PROMPT.md first. It is written for language models.

Example: src/examples/ticket-triage.

## ai-agent4j (core library, about 440 KB)

- [README](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/README.md): ReAct agents, tools, memory, RAG, personas, skills, voice, budgets
- [ReAct Agent Guide](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/ReAct-Agent-Guide.md): the plan, action and observation loop; approvals; events
- [Providers and the Uniform Contract](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Providers-and-the-Uniform-Contract.md): switching models by name; what every provider guarantees
- [Creating Custom Tools](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Creating-Custom-Tools.md): the `Tool` interface, `requiresApproval`, effect contracts (`Effectful`, `EffectJournal`)
- [Native Tool Calling](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Native-Tool-Calling.md): `ReActAgent.toolCalling(AUTO|NATIVE|TEXT)`, `Tool.getParametersSchema()` / `ToolSchema`, `LLMRequest.tools`, `LLMResponse.getToolCalls()`; Gemini and Claude use structured tool calls, Sarvam and Ollama the text protocol
- [Secret Store](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Secret-Store.md): `SecretStore`, `SecretRef`, `EncryptedFileSecretStore`, `MasterKey`; providers and tools fetch keys per request; Loom `secret.NAME` and `weave secrets`
- [Creating Tasks](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Creating-Tasks.md): the `Task` interface, deterministic steps with no model (`TaskContext`, `TaskResult`, `TaskRegistry`); run from Loom with `run`
- [Budgets and Rate Limits](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Budgets-and-Rate-Limits.md): `Budget` caps checked before each call; parsing provider 429s into exact reset times
- [Loom context and compaction](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/LOOM_GUIDE.md): `context { compact: chain(...) }` block per agent, windows files (`--context-windows`, `<script>.windows`), `.loct` files for your own strategies (`--loct`), trace events `context`/`compaction`/`model_call`/`tool_call` (with `reach`)/`failure`/`guard` (a failed task or delegate; `run_end` names what broke the run), `ObservableRun.stats()`, `memory { max_tokens }` to bound the shared transcript, `weave audit` context section
- [Guide chapter 14: context and compaction](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/docs/guide/14-context-and-compaction.md): when an agent needs a `context` block, which strategies to chain, where the window comes from, and the three signals to watch (`weave guide 14`).
- [Guide chapter 15: steer, stop and supervise a running workflow](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/docs/guide/15-steer-stop-and-supervise.md): `steerable`/`streaming`/`reasoning` agents, `on_stopped { }` and `intervention { }` (outcomes `use partial`, `skip`, `discard`, `retry`, `suspend`, `conclude`, `ask`, `rewind to` a declared checkpoint, with `_stop.reason|note|kind|phase|partial|changed|origin`), `supervise Agent { when looping(N) | tool_failing(Tool, N) | context > P% | steps > N { steer "…" | wrap_up | cancel } }`, reaching a running workflow (`weave run --steer-via console`, a chat through `weave daemon`, `LoomRun`), `weave audit` rule LA18 (`weave guide 15`). Also `shared_prompt: "…"` / `shared_prompt: prompt "id"` at the top of a script puts one text first in every agent's prompt.
- [Steering, Streaming and Hooks](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Steering-Streaming-and-Hooks.md): `RunHandle` (steer, pause, resume, cancel, wrap up from another thread), streaming and reasoning deltas, `ToolHook` and argument validation, `RunHook` (check the question, each model call, the final answer; fails closed), `DelegateTaskTool` depth limit and tool grants
- [Skills](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/docs/PUBLISHING_SKILL.md): `llm4j-harness-design` designs the harness around an autonomous workflow and writes a `HARNESS.md`; `llm4j-workflow-guide` builds, tests, secures and ships a workflow; `llm4j-loom-deployer` runs it observed (the security decisions, the rules file, the Fabric server, launching both, reading the pages). `weave guide --install-skill` installs all three (`--skill harness|workflow|deployer` for one).
- [Telemetry and Statistics](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Telemetry-and-Statistics.md): `ErrorCategory` (one failure vocabulary), `ToolException`, `Tool.isFailure`, `ModelCallEvent`/`ToolCallEvent`, `LatencyStats` percentiles, `StatsCollector`, `CallTrace`; `ReActAgent.Builder.clock`, `AgentResult.getStats()`; the agent reports every tool call and model call (both loops), including retries, waits and fail-overs
- [Context and Compaction](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Context-and-Compaction.md): `ContextCompactor` (a functional interface), built-in `none`/`drop_oldest`/`trim_tool_results`/`summarize`/`chain`, discovery by name, `ContextPolicy`, `ContextWindows`, `ContextOverflowException` (compact harder and retry once), `ConversationHistory.builder().maxTokens(..).compaction(..)`, `ContextWindows.defaults()`; `ReActAgent.builder().contextWindow(..).compaction(..)` and `AgentEventListener.onContextUsage/onCompaction` work in both agent loops (native tool calling and the text protocol)
- [Classification](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Classification.md): `Classifier` (a functional interface: `ClassifyRequest` with named `choice`/`yesNo`/`score` questions in, a `ClassifyResult` of typed answers out; a label is always one of the request's labels, anything else is a `ClassificationException`), `Classifier.using(LLMClient)` / `LlmClassifier.builder(client).samples(n).withRationale(..).maxOutputTokens(..)`, `Classifier.using(ClassificationProvider)` for backends that answer typed questions directly, `observed(listener)`; answers say `calibrated()` (a chat model's never is). eval4j: `llmJudged(..).classifier(c)` (yes/no, or `.graded(true)`), `ClassifierComparison` (labelled cases, named contenders, accuracy/ECE/Brier/selective accuracy/latency/cost/agreement), `ScriptedClassifier` test double. `JevProvider` (io.github.llm4j.provider.typesafe; `ClassificationProvider`, calibrated, `Classifier.using(new JevProvider(cfg))`) and `ClassifierResolver` (`Jev/jev-latest` or any chat model name, one string to switch). Loom `intentclassify` is coming in the same release
- [MCP Integration](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/MCP-Integration.md) and [OpenAPI Tool](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/OpenAPI-Tool.md): tools from MCP servers and REST specs
- [Memory and Persistence](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Memory-and-Persistence.md), [Semantic Memory](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/SEMANTIC_MEMORY.md), [RAG](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/RAG-Support.md), [Knowledge Graphs](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Knowledge-Graphs.md)
- [Agent Skills](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Agent-Skills-Guide.md), [Personas](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Agent-Personas.md), [Prompt Registry](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/Prompt-Registry-Guide.md)
- [xAI: Beyond Black Boxes](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/wiki/xAI_BEYOND_BLACK_BOXES.md): audit trails, PII masking (`MaskingLLMClient`), bias monitoring, confidence
- [Module llms.txt](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j/llms.txt): the core library in more detail

## ai-agent4j-tools (tools built for a hostile caller)

- [Tools documentation](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/README.md): `webhook` (Slack, Discord, Teams), `email`, `http`, `file`, `shell` and read-only `sql`. Each has allow-lists, internal-address blocking, size and time caps, and secrets scrubbed from results. A journal makes sure a crash never repeats a send. Use them from Java or from Loom.
- [Safety model](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/safety.md): what a hostile call tries, what stops it, and what the tools don't do
- [Writing a tool](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j-tools/docs/writing-a-tool.md): building your own on the same contracts

## Loom (workflows that run for days)

- [Loom overview](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/README.md) and [Why Loom?](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/WHY_LOOM.md): long-running, unattended workflows; comparison with LangGraph
- [Language guide](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/LOOM_GUIDE.md): every statement and command, with examples checked by tests
- [Budgets, Pausing and Scheduling](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/BUDGETS_AND_SCHEDULING.md): budgets, rate-limit pauses, schedules and triggers that survive restarts
- [Agentic workflows with Loom and Engram](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/docs/AGENTIC_WORKFLOWS_GUIDE.md)

Language at a glance:
- **Declarations:** `agent` (model, system, tools, `approve:`, `guard { pii, bias }`, `budget`, `memory`, `output_schema`, `max_iterations`); `tool` (`use: webhook | email | http | file | shell | sql | serpapi | openapi | class | ...`, secrets only as `env.NAME` or `secret.NAME`; `openapi` `auth_value` can be `invoker.NAME`, the credential of the person running the workflow, supplied per run through `InvokerCredentials`); `knowledge`; `provider`; `persona`; `budget`; `schedule`; `decision`.
- **Statements:** `delegate "task" to Agent -> result expecting { field: type }`; `run Task(arg = value) -> result` (a deterministic Java `Task`: no model, journaled, never repeated by a crash if it changes things; a model cannot call it); `broadcast`; `handoff`; `alt (cond) { } else { }`; `loop until (cond) max N on_exhausted { }`; `for each item in list { }` and `parallel for each` (the target agent may come from the item, but only a declared agent); `human_prompt`; `guardrail (PII) { } on_violation { }`; `call`; `note`.
- **Durability:** every step is journaled (memory, file or SQL); a run pauses on rate limits, budgets and people, and resumes without repeating sends.
- **Ending a run, handing back a value, asking whether a step worked:** `halt "reason {var}"` (ends the whole run on purpose: not a failure, so nothing retries or handles it; status `halted`, exit code 6); `set name = value` and `return { verdict: "PASSED", detail: "..." }` (values: text, number, true/false, another variable, or an object; `return` is `set result` then the end of the workflow, so a `call` hands it back); `x is ok` / `x is not ok` in `alt`, `loop until` and `rewind when` (true only when the `run` step's task calls its outcome ok, `Task.okOutcomes()`, default `ok`; fails closed; a step only described in a simulated run counts as ok).
- **Structured answers are checked:** an agent's answer is read against its `output_schema` / `expecting` (JSON found inside a fence or chatter; every field present and of its type; enum words exact). A wrong answer is a failed attempt, retried with a correction (one free correction, then `retry N`), and the step fails into `on_failure` when they run out; it is never passed on as raw text.
- **Checkpoints, rewind and fork:** `checkpoint name`; `rewind to name when (cond) at most N times carrying x = "..." side effects: ask first | keep | repeat`. `weave timeline | rewind | reset | fork` operate runs from outside; `--effects simulate` re-runs with nothing performed.
- **Earned autonomy:** `decision Name { proposed by, choices, group cases by, dangerous mistake, ask, trust { start at watch, never go above suggest, to suggest: after N cases, agreeing at least P%, ... } }` with `decide Name -> verdict`. The agent moves `watch` → `suggest` → `act` on a blind, statistically conservative record, and back down. `weave autonomy status | history | promote | demote | freeze | outcome | verify` operates it (`verify` checks that nobody edited the record of levels), and `weave replay` tests a changed prompt or model on past cases with nothing sent.
- **Ladders:** `ladder Name(params) { rung watch { mode: blind } rung suggest { mode: confirm climb when history.count >= 100 and history.rate(agrees).lower95 >= 0.9 } rung act { mode: autonomous climb when ... slip to suggest when ... sample 5% blind escalate when case.amount > 200 } climbing needs approval from NAME }`, `measure edit_size(c) = distance(c.proposal.value, c.response.final)`, bound with `ladder: Name(param: value)` and `ceiling: rung` in a `decision` (which may `proposes: post` instead of `choices:`). Standard measures: `import "loom/autonomy"`. Read back with `weave ladder describe`.
- **Answering from a phone:** `--ask-via telegram` (or `<store>/channel.json`) sends questions and approvals to a chat; only allowlisted users can answer, and approvals need the question's code. `weave questions` and `weave answer` do the same from a terminal; `weave tick` or `weave daemon` resume the run.
- **Commands:** `weave run | check | resume | tick | daemon | observe | triggers | schedule | package | timeline | rewind | reset | fork | why | autonomy | ladder | replay | questions | answer | audit | review | rules | graph | symbols | explain | next | eval | test | serve | init | guide | secrets`.
- **Tools, models and context in the run view:** per-tool health (`healthy`/`degraded`/`failing`) with success rate, failures by category and per-agent breakdown, `RunRegistry.toolRollup()` across runs, per-model and per-agent context statistics, and incidents for context nearly full, truncated answers, compaction thrash, collapsing tool success rate and latency spikes (rules in the `.inspect` file); see wiki/Observability-Incidents-and-Rules.md.
- **Watching runs:** with the optional `loom-inspect` add-on, `--observe` serves a live page (a run's context gauge and compaction timeline, a tools-and-tasks health table, a security view; pause, suspend and stop and secret rotation only for a signed-in admin), and `--observe-fabric <url> --observe-name <name>` reports to a Fabric server (`loom-fabric`); events are kept in a local outbox so a down server never affects a workflow. See docs/OBSERVABILITY.md, wiki/Fabric-Server.md and the Loom guide, "Watching runs live".
- **Prompt files:** an agent's prompt can be a markdown file: `prompt: "researcher"` (latest) or `prompt: "researcher@v2"`, from `prompts/<id>.md` or `prompts/<id>/vN.md` beside the script (or `prompts: "./dir"`, or `--prompts dir`). `--prompt researcher@v1` pins a version for one run, for a fair A/B. `weave check` finds missing files and versions; `weave audit` lists which prompt each agent runs. Example: `src/examples/newsletter`.
- **Testing the logic:** `weave test script.loom` runs the cases of `tests/*.test.yaml` with scripted models, so branches, routes and results are tested with no model, no key, no network and no spend. A case gives `input`, the `models:` answers (a text, a list in order, a `when` list chosen by the task text, or a typed map; a classifier gets a label for each question), and `expect:` (`result`, `route`, `calls`, `never`, `context`, `models_used`, `final`) with matchers such as `contains`, `matches`, `one_of`, `gt`. A model call nobody scripted fails the case and names the agent, the call and the task (`--lenient` allows a neutral reply). `--check` validates the files against the script (a renamed agent shows the nearest name), `--steps` lists the step names a test can use, `--show-case NAME` prints the merged case, `--case GLOB` and `--fail-fast` select and stop. `fail:` injects failures (rate_limit, timeout, server_error, invalid_output, tool_error, refused, quota), `tools:`/`tasks:` script tools and tasks (acting tools only record effects), `humans:`/`resume:` answer and continue a suspended run, `clock:` makes time virtual, `steer:`/`stop:` (after_call or after_chunk) and `stream:` script a person steering a streaming agent. `--coverage` lists steps no case reached, `--min-coverage N` fails below N percent, `--format text|json|junit|tap`, `--tag`/`--exclude-tag`, `--shuffle --seed`, `--parallel`, `--watch`. From Java, `LoomTest`/`LoomRunAssert` run the same cases and `LoomTest.cases(path)` gives the test files as JUnit cases. `weave init` ships a passing `tests/` in every starter. Exit 0 all passed, 1 a case failed, 2 it could not run. This tests the workflow's logic; whether the agents answer well is `weave eval`.
- **Evaluation:** `weave eval script.loom` runs a golden dataset (`eval/golden/<agent>.yaml`, `workflow.yaml`, optional `dataset.yaml` and `fixtures.yaml`) and reports passed, failed and unjudged; `--init` creates a starter, `--check` validates with no model, `--mock` runs the wiring for free (content checks are then unjudged), a real run needs a cap and asks first. Scenarios: `input`, `expected_output_contains`, `expected_tools`, `rubric`, `expect`, `dimensions`, `tags`. Evaluation is optional. Example: `src/examples/newsletter/eval/golden`.
- **Editor engine:** `weave serve --stdio` is one long-lived process that answers an editor's `loom/check`, `loom/graph`, `loom/review`, `loom/symbols` and `loom/explainRule` requests (JSON-RPC with Content-Length framing, unsaved buffers, a cache keyed by file content, a workspace boundary). It runs nothing and writes nothing. The protocol is in `docs/serve/PROTOCOL.md`.
- **Starting out:** `weave init pipeline|approval|classifier <dir>` creates a small working project (script, prompts as files, golden dataset, README); `--with-java-tests` adds a Maven test module for the Java path. `weave check script.loom --no-env` validates with no model and no keys (`--format json`, `--strict`). `weave guide [page]` prints the guide from inside the jar (chapters 1 to 10, `readme`, `loom`, `llms`); `weave guide --install-skill` adds the agent skill to a project; `weave guide recipes` has tested changes to the starter. For a developer's own machine, keys go in a gitignored `.env` beside the script (`weave init` writes `.env.example` and `.gitignore`; `run`, `check`, `eval` and `next` read it; `--env-file`, `--no-env-file`); a deployed application uses the secret store. `weave explain script.loom` describes a script in plain English and `weave next` says what to do next in a project; both are free (no model, no key).
- **Why:** `weave why RUN_DIR [STEP|NODE|LINE]` explains a run from its journal: each choice it made (a condition, a loop going round or leaving, a list, a classifier's answer, a rewind, a failure taken over) with the condition as written, the values it was made of and where each came from, and the way it did not go; asked about a line it says why that statement ran, or which choice kept it out and what would have let it in. The run is replayed over a copy of its journal with no model, tool, task, person or network, so it is exact, the same every time, needs none of the run's keys and writes nothing. `--format text|md|json`, `--all`, `--since STEP`; a script that changed since the run is refused unless `--script old.loom` is given. Where the journal and the script disagree it says where (diverged at STEP) and never invents a value.
- **Symbols:** `weave symbols script.loom` prints, as JSON, what a script and its imports define (agents, workflows, tools, classifiers, personas, providers, decisions, checkpoints, prompt files), where each name is used (with its role: delegate target, tool use, call, rewind, classify, ...), and what each variable holds (a classifier's record with its enum labels, an agent's `output_schema`, `unknown` when it cannot be known). Ranges are 0-based lines and UTF-16 columns. A script with a syntax error still answers for the parts that read, with the problems listed. It runs nothing and needs no keys; it is the index behind go to definition, rename and completion in the editor.
- **Workflow graph:** `weave graph script.loom` prints the workflows of a script and its imports as nodes and edges (JSON, or `--format mermaid`), with the settings written on each step. It runs nothing and needs no keys.
- **Security review:** `weave audit script.loom` reports what each agent can reach. It flags one agent that holds untrusted content, private data and a way out; it also flags unapproved effects and risky settings, mapping every finding to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025). It exits 1 on a high finding.
- **Review:** `weave review script.loom` is one ranked list across security (the audit above), validity (`weave check`) and further lenses, each finding with why it matters and what to do. It is advisory: it exits 1 only with `--fail-on high|medium|low|info` (or `fail-on =` in `review.properties` beside the script). `--lens` chooses lenses, `--format json|md`, `--explain RULE` explains a rule. It runs nothing and needs no keys. Rules are data: `weave rules list | facts | check | test | new | add | explain --at` works with rule packs offline, and a project pins packs in `review.properties` (`packs = core@1, acme@2.0.1 sha256:…`); packs are never downloaded. `weave review` also writes SARIF (`--format sarif`), takes Java rules from a jar you name (`--rules-jar`), and a `RULE.suppress = place "reason"` line in `review.properties` sets one finding aside (without a reason it is itself a finding). The report says what each workflow is estimated to cost, typical and worst case, from the script alone (`--prices FILE` for money, `--assume loop.iterations=5` to change an assumption, `--explain cost` for how, `--calibrate RUN_DIR` to compare with a real run); an unbounded loop is reported as unbounded, never as a number. The same card says how long each workflow takes (typical and worst, with waits for people and timers listed) and how many sends and writes it can cause (a retry repeats an effect; `--assume latency.standard=8` changes a latency); `LC08` finds steps that could run in parallel, `LC09`/`LC10` check the time against limits you declare, and the optional testability lens (`--lens +testability`) reads `tests/*.test.yaml`. Four more optional lenses are off until asked (`--lens +governance|maintainability|oversight|blast-radius`, or `--lens all`): governance (typo'd or deprecated models, unversioned prompts), maintainability (long prompts, large workflows, duplicate agents, a number repeated in conditions), oversight (a decision with no trust block before an action, noisy approvals, too many questions per run, free-text answers compared exactly) and blast radius (acting steps in unbounded repeats, too many effects per run, scheduled workflows with no budget per day). Findings can be handled without editing code by hand: `--fix` applies the safe fixes (each result is checked: the script still loads and no new high finding appears; `--dry-run` prints the diff), `--accept FINGERPRINT|RULE --reason "…"` records why a finding is fine in `review.properties` (with `--scope`, `--until`), a finding that has several reasonable resolutions lists **options** (in the JSON report and as `options:` in the text report) and the developer decides: `--assist` walks them interactively (choose, answer the questions, see the diff, confirm), and `--fix-finding FINGERPRINT --option ID --set name=value [--dry-run] [--yes]` does one non-interactively (`--yes` for an option that needs thought); `--baseline-write` records today's findings so only new ones count, and `--noise-report` says which rules are accepted almost everywhere. `weave run` and `weave package` print one advisory line to standard error when findings are open (`--review-notice`, `notice =` in `review.properties`, `LOOM_REVIEW_NOTICE`); findings never block them.

## Other modules

- [Engram](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/engram/engram-core/README.md): long-term memory as extracted facts and a short per-turn briefing instead of a growing transcript
- [Addons](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/ai-agent4j-addons/README.md): local embeddings (ONNX, DJL) and persistent vector stores (pgvector, Pinecone)
- [eval4j](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/eval4j/README.md): AssertJ assertions on what agents did; LLM-as-judge conditions (correctness, groundedness, hallucination, bias, toxicity); YAML datasets; pass-rate thresholds; prompt optimisation; all in `mvn test`
- [eval4j-report](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/eval4j-report/README.md): free, local dashboard for eval4j runs: quality dimensions with goals, run comparison with judge noise, cost-aware profiles, agent traces, Loom trajectories; one self-contained HTML file plus a CSP-safe static edition
- [Loom CTK](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ctk/README.md): conformance tests for Loom runtimes
- [VS Code extension](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/vscode-loom/README.md): checks from the language's own parser, the workflow graph, a review panel (findings, cost and fixes you decide on), and go to definition, rename, completion and hover that know your agents and variables; one `weave serve` engine per window, no network

## Examples

- [GetViral](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/examples/getviral/README.md): twelve agents, one Loom workflow, every module; one idea in, a ready-to-post pack for X, Instagram Reels and YouTube out
- [Hexamind Hub](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/examples/hexamind-hub/README.md): six agents with distinct personalities debating a problem live
- [Nirmaan Yantra](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/examples/nirmaan-yantra/README.md): an autonomous software factory from a one-line prompt
- [Kingini](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/examples/kingini/README.md): a voice-first companion in Malayalam on Sarvam
- [Daily digest sample](https://github.com/srijithunni7182/llm4j/blob/main/src/loom/ai-agent4j-loom/samples/digest/digest.loom): a scheduled Loom workflow using the generic tools
